title: Automorphism pullback commutes with completion with a unique unit normalization
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring and $d$ a Noetherian adic coefficient datum with finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq A$, additive-torsion $A/I$, and finite perfect quotients $A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Work on the chosen small pro-etale site, with $A_X=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_X$, coefficient universe one above the scheme universe, and $\mathcal D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$. Fix any finite tuple $a$ generating $I$. Let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be the Koszul completion reflector of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], with the explicit intrinsic unit $\eta_M:M\to LM$ of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] on specified cochain representatives; $\mathcal C$ is the full subcategory where this unit is invertible.

Let $e:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ be a scheme automorphism. Give ordinary module pullback the coefficient isomorphism $c_e:e^{-1}A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ induced by the constant quotient comparisons and the inverse-image limit comparison [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $H=Le^*$ be the resulting ordinary derived pullback and $G=Re_*$ its module right adjoint, using the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Both $H$ and $G$ preserve $\mathcal C$, and their adjoint equivalence restricts to $\mathcal C$. For every $M\in\mathcal D$ there is a unique isomorphism
$$c_M:H(LM)\xrightarrow{\sim}L(HM),\qquad H(\eta_M);c_M=\eta_{HM}.$$
These claims hold for the actual completed coefficient sheaf and the specified intrinsic units, for every finite generating tuple and every representative, without a constructibility or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text:
Put $R=A_X$ and $P_n=A/I^n$. For each $n$, the isomorphism-of-sites lemma gives the constant-ring isomorphism $c_n:e^{-1}(P_n)_X\to(P_n)_X$ and its naturality for quotient maps. Its inverse-image limit comparison therefore gives
$$c_e:e^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_n e^{-1}(P_n)_X\xrightarrow{\varprojlim c_n}R.$$
This is precisely the map specified by the components in the completed-pullback definition, since both have components $c_n e^{-1}(\pi_n)$. For every $b\in A$, the definition of the constant structure map sends the constant residue of $b$ to itself. Projecting to every $P_n$ thus shows that $c_e$ takes the pulled-back global scalar $b$ to the scalar $b$ in $R$. In particular it fixes every $a_j$ and every $a_j^m$. The construction for $e^{-1}$ is inverse to this construction: on each finite quotient both composites send every constant residue to itself, and equality on all projections is equality of maps into the limit.

source.place: Functoriality of the pro-etale site, Tag 09A5; explicit completed coefficient comparison in the blueprint tensor-Frobenius sentence

proof.text: Let $T$ denote module pullback along $e$ with $c_e$. Use the site-relabeling model of the isomorphism lemma: its underlying abelian sheaf at $(U\xrightarrow{u}X)$ is $M(U\xrightarrow{eu}X)$. The scalar-extension-along-a-ring-isomorphism lemma identifies $e^{-1}M\otimes_{e^{-1}R}R$ with that abelian sheaf, endowed with the action $s\cdot m=c_e^{-1}(s)m$; explicitly $m\otimes s\mapsto c_e^{-1}(s)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Relabeling by $e^{-1}$, with the inverse coefficient comparison of Step 1, gives an inverse module functor $S$. The two composite identifications are the site-equivalence identifications on underlying abelian sheaves, and are linear because the coefficient comparisons compose to the identity. They are therefore natural module isomorphisms $ST\cong1$ and $TS\cong1$. Both functors are additive and exact: the underlying inverse-image equivalences are exact, and changing the action by an invertible ring map changes no kernel or cokernel. The module-adjunction lemma identifies the right adjoint of this actual tensor-formula $T$ with the actual module direct image $e_*$. As $S$ is also a right adjoint (the displayed inverse equivalence supplies its Hom bijection), these adjunctions identify $e_*\cong S$.

Apply the exact-functor derived-category lemma to $T,S$. Their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce inverse functors on the unbounded derived category; the units, counits and triangle identities descend because they already hold on complexes. Since both ordinary functors are exact, these are the ordinary derived functors $H=Le^*$ and $G=Re_*$. In particular the descended adjunction is the one induced from the specified module adjunction, not an independently chosen equivalence. No boundedness or resolution-compatibility hypothesis is needed for applying an exact functor termwise.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; applied to the exact module equivalence of Step 2

proof.text:
Fix the generating tuple and any cochain representative $C$ of $M$. Use $Q_m$, $q_{m+1,m}$ and $M_m(C)=C\otimes_RQ_m$ exactly as in the intrinsic-completion definition. In the exterior-basis description, $Q_m^{-k}$ is the finite free module with basis the $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$; its differential entries are $0$ or $\pm a_j^m$. Its transition on the subset $J$ is multiplication by $\prod_{j\in J}a_j$, and the degree-zero inclusion has coefficient $1$. Applying $T$ and identifying $T(R)$ with $R$ by $c_e$ fixes all these matrices by Step 1. Hence it identifies $TQ_m$ with $Q_m$, including transitions and inclusions. Since tensoring $C$ with this finite free complex is degreewise a finite direct sum of copies of terms of $C$, the same identifications and additivity give chain isomorphisms
$$\alpha_m:T(M_m(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}M_m(TC).$$
They commute with differentials $d_C\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_{Q_m}$ and satisfy $\alpha_mT(t_m)=t'_m\alpha_{m+1}$: every summand has the identical sign and scalar on both sides. This computation uses ordinary tensor complexes on the actual representatives.

source.place: second sentence, completed pullback in tensor Frobenius; explicit Koszul factors, transitions and total-complex differential

proof.text:
Write $B=B(C)$, $B'=B(TC)$ and $f=1-t$, $f'=1-t'$ as in the completion definition. The equivalence $T$ preserves products: for each module $N$, the inverse equivalence gives $\operatorname{Hom}(N,T\prod M_m)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(SN,\prod M_m)\cong\prod\operatorname{Hom}(N,TM_m)$, with the indicated projections. Thus the maps whose components are $\alpha_mT(\operatorname{pr}_m)$ give a chain isomorphism $\beta:T B\to B'$. After projection to the $m$-th term, the identity $\beta T(f)=f'\beta$ is exactly the transition identity of Step 4. On the two summands of the specified mapping fiber put
$$\gamma_C^i=\beta^i\oplus\beta^{i-1}:T(F(C)^i)\longrightarrow F(TC)^i.$$
Using $d_F(x,y)=(d_Bx,fx-d_By)$, the second component of the chain-map equation is $\beta fx-\beta d_By=f'\beta x-d_{B'}\beta y$; the first is the chain-map equation for $\beta$. These prove that $\gamma_C$ is a chain isomorphism; its inverse uses the inverse of $\beta$ on both summands. These are maps between the specified product and mapping-fiber complexes, rather than unspecified maps obtained from distinguished triangles.

source.place: second sentence, completed pullback in tensor Frobenius; product comparison and mapping-fiber comparison in the parent definition

proof.text:
Let $u_C:C\to B(C)$ have components $1\otimes\iota_m$. Step 4 preserves $\iota_m$, so projection to each factor gives $\beta T(u_C)=u_{TC}$. Consequently
$$\gamma_C\,T\bigl(c\mapsto(u_C(c),0)\bigr)=\bigl(x\mapsto(u_{TC}(x),0)\bigr).$$
This is the desired unit square as an equality of chain maps. Every $\alpha_m$, $\beta$ and $\gamma_C$ commutes with a chain map $C\to C'$: on each finite summand the operation is that chain map, and on each product it is its projected component. The intrinsic-completion definition interprets $F$ and its unit on the derived category, and Step 3 interprets $T$ there. Naturality therefore descends through quasi-isomorphisms, giving an isomorphism $c_M:H(LM)\to L(HM)$ with $c_M\circ H(\eta_M)=\eta_{HM}$. This works for any chosen representative of $M$; it does not choose a strict representative for an arbitrary derived morphism.

source.place: second sentence, completed pullback in tensor Frobenius; intrinsic augmentation and base Step 8 unit normalization

proof.text: If $M$ is in $\mathcal C$, then $H(\eta_M)$ and $c_M$ are invertible, so the unit square makes $\eta_{HM}$ invertible. Thus $H$ preserves $\mathcal C$. Repeat Steps 1--6 for the inverse scheme automorphism: it fixes the same scalars and has the same small-site equivalence and inverse completed-ring comparison. Its derived module transport $S$ therefore preserves $\mathcal C$ as well. Step 3 identifies $S$ with $G$; being in $\mathcal C$ is invariant under isomorphism: by the strict-limit comparison [lem-weil-pbc-completed-fiber-strict-limit-comparison], after the explicit module equivalence $F$ to the transported site with ring $\mathcal O$ and the images $b$ of the generators, $F(\eta_K)$ followed by an isomorphism $e_K$ is the reflector unit of $FK$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], so $\eta_K$ is invertible exactly when that natural reflector unit is, and the latter property is invariant under isomorphism. Hence $G$ preserves $\mathcal C$. As this is a full subcategory, the adjunction Hom bijections, unit and counit of Step 3 restrict to it. The latter maps remain invertible and retain their triangle identities. They give the asserted restricted adjoint equivalence.

source.place: second sentence, completed pullback in tensor Frobenius; base Step 8 completeness predicates and adjoint equivalence

proof.text: It remains to show that the unit square determines the comparison. Transport through the strict-limit comparison [lem-weil-pbc-completed-fiber-strict-limit-comparison]: for every $K$ there is $e_K:F(LK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{compl}(FK)$ with $F(\eta_K);e_K$ the reflector unit of $FK$ on the transported site, $F$ an equivalence. Hence, by the reflector lemma, $K$ is in $\mathcal C$ exactly when $FK$ is locally derived complete, $LK$ is in $\mathcal C$, and for $K'$ in $\mathcal C$ composition with $\eta_K$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(LK,K')\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,K')$ (conjugate the reflector bijection by $e_K$ and full faithfulness of $F$). Put $N=L(HM)$, which is complete. By Step 7, $GN$ is complete. For any $v,w:H(LM)\to N$ such that $vH(\eta_M)=wH(\eta_M)$, take adjuncts under $H\dashv G$. Naturality of the adjunction bijection gives $\widetilde v\eta_M=\widetilde w\eta_M$, with $\widetilde v,\widetilde w:LM\to GN$. By the transported reflector bijection above, composition with $\eta_M$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(LM,GN)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,GN)$. Its injectivity gives $\widetilde v=\widetilde w$, and the adjunction bijection gives $v=w$. Applied to any proposed comparison and the isomorphism constructed in Step 6, this proves uniqueness, even among all maps satisfying the square. The construction was performed for an arbitrary finite generating tuple, including the empty tuple when it generates $I$, and on an arbitrary complex, so the assertion holds for every such tuple and representative.
